Infections in immunocompromised patients Patients with a defective immune system are at particular risk of infection. Primary immune deficiency is rare, whereas secondary deficiency is more common: immuno- suppressive therapy, cancer and its treatment, HIV infec- tion, and splenectomy may all cause neutropenia and im- paired humoral and cellular immunity in varying degrees. The risk of infection is linked to the duration and severity of neutropenia. Most protozoal infections present in a more severe form in immunocompromised patients than in immunocompetent patients. Those of particular concern in patients with HIV infection include Cryptosporidiosis (above), Isosporiasis (below), Leishmaniasis (below), Mi- crosporidiosis (below), and Toxoplasmosis (below).
